style.vernacular: Dense continental-scale metropolis: Paulista modernist exposed-concrete and glass towers; endless mid-rise concrete-frame apartment blocks rendered in cream, ochre and grey; self-built red brick and block houses with slab roofs in the periphery; surviving neocolonial and Italian-immigrant brick and stucco buildings with clay-tile hipped roofs in older districts (Luz, Mooca, Horto); tile-clad facades; graffiti murals in Vila Madalena; roads lined with broadleaf trees and palms.
style.ornament: Exposed board-marked concrete and brise-soleil (Paulista school); ceramic tile panels; neocolonial wide eaves with brackets, curved pediments and arches; painted street murals; butterfly roofs and primary-colour accents (Artigas).

sources.what: neocolonial style with clay-tile roofs and arches
Paulista modernist house: concrete butterfly roof, painted brick, glass band
white-tile and glass contemporary stadium
colonial origins, neoclassical theatre, Niemeyer concrete modernism (Edificio Copan)
